name: KIDs S&C
description: Colecție de 6 volume livrate pe rând. Fiecare volum: carte de povești (în fiecare limbă aleasă) și carte de colorat, cu aceleași scene și personaje.
brief_en: A collection of 6 volumes. Every volume is a full-colour storybook plus a matching black-and-white colouring book, each exactly 12 content pages plus a cover. The colouring book redraws the storybook's scenes and characters identically as line art, so the child uses the storybook as a colour reference.

rubric.text: Age fit: vocabulary, sentence length and conflict intensity match the age profile exactly
Coherence: clear beginning, middle and end; every page moves the story forward
Continuity: characters, names, looks and world match the Story Bible
Read-aloud rhythm: pleasant to read aloud, no awkward phrasing
Illustratability: each page has one clear, visually distinct, drawable moment; consecutive pages never look alike
Colouring suitability: scenes are not too crowded for the age
Safety and values: nothing frightening beyond the age, no stereotypes, positive values
Format: exact page count; text length close to the age guideline (a variation of about a third is fine when the story needs it)
Cast: the main character leads; returning characters are re-introduced naturally; the volume follows the cast plan
Page turns: a few real reveals, the rest quieter; every turn connects to the previous page
Reveal pacing: nothing is shown before the page where it is discovered
Repetition with variation (rule of three, a refrain) that invites the child to join in
Agency: the main character drives the key actions; secondary characters never dominate
Ending: warm and complete, no artificial sequel teaser
Clarity: no scene a parent could misread (e.g. friends sleeping together); unambiguous pronouns; natural, non-redundant wording
Physical causality: each page has one clear event whose cause and effect make sense
No procedural or adult safety-manual language in the story
World rules respected: natural light and weather are not presented as magic

prompts.bible:
TASK: write the Story Bible of the collection. The bible is the single source of truth: every later text and every illustration copies from it.

CREATIVE BRIEF: {{brief}}
SERIES ARC: {{series}}
CLIENT'S STORY FOR VOLUME 1 (may be empty; its characters must be in the cast with the looks it describes): {{input.seed_story}}
AGE PROFILE: {{age_profile}} (max_characters is a guideline for how many characters feel comfortable in one volume, not a hard cap for the whole collection)
CAST RULES: exactly ONE main character (role "main") who carries the whole collection, plus secondary characters (role "secondary") who can appear in some volumes, step back and return later. Give every secondary a small personal arc across the collection.

Define the cast, the recurring key objects, the world and the illustration style.
Character design rules: build each character on shape language (round, soft forms for friendly and young characters; no sharp, threatening angles for heroes); the silhouette must be recognisable in solid black at small print size; keep 1-2 signature features (e.g. an exact number of spots, one accessory) that never change; state exact proportions (head-to-body ratio). For every character give the expression range used in the books, behaviour rules (what they never do) and forbidden visual deviations (e.g. sharp teeth, a different number of spots, adult proportions, clothing changes). Recurring key objects and locations get ids and one English canonical_description each.
Anatomy and interaction (critical for image generation): for every character state the stance, limb count, what the extremities look like, and HOW this character can hold or carry objects in a way true to its body (e.g. a quadruped: in its mouth or beak, balanced on its horns or back, pinned under a front foot, nudged with the nose; NEVER with a human-like grasping hand or fingers). "never" lists anatomy that must not appear (e.g. "human-like hands", "fingers", "a fifth limb").
"invariants": short, countable facts an inspector can check on every page (e.g. "exactly 3 coral spots on the left flank", "exactly 3 horns: 2 brow horns + 1 nose horn", "lavender frill", "cream belly and toes"). Objects get invariants too (e.g. "smooth, shiny, rounded, fits in two small hands").
Species: name a real species ONLY if the design clearly supports it ("species_certainty": "certain"); otherwise "indeterminate_stylized" and the text must never claim a species for that character.
World rules: state whether magic exists ("none" by default) and how light effects work, so a sparkle is never read as magic when it is sunlight. Visual descriptions must be concrete and unambiguous so that an illustrator draws each character identically on 150 pages: type/species, body shape and proportions, face, hair or fur, outfit, exact colours as hex codes, 2-3 distinctive features that never change. "canonical_description" is ONE dense English sentence that will be pasted verbatim into every image prompt.
ILLUSTRATION STYLE IS FIXED by the art director. Copy this text verbatim into style_guide.style_block and choose palette, lighting and mood that suit the story within it: {{style.style_block}}
CLIENT CHARACTERS (may be empty): {{refs.characters}}. If present, they MUST be in the cast with the SAME id, and their visual description and canonical_description must match exactly; you may give them the suggested name or a better one.

Names in {{input.language}}; canonical_description and style_block in English; everything else in {{ui_language}}.

prompts.script:
TASK: write one volume of a premium children's picture book collection.

COLLECTION CONTEXT (the same for every volume):
CREATIVE BRIEF: {{brief}}
SERIES THROUGH-LINE: {{series.through_line}}
AGE PROFILE (guidance, not a hard rule): {{age_profile}}
STORY BIBLE (use only these characters, names and looks): {{bible_volume}}

Rules:
- Exactly {{structure.pages}} pages plus a cover. Each page is one clear, visually distinct moment; the story has a real beginning, middle and satisfying end.
- Page "text" in {{input.language}}, about {{age_profile.max_chars}} characters per page as a GUIDELINE (it may vary by roughly a third when a scene needs it; never pad or cut awkwardly), following the age profile for sentence length, vocabulary, dialogue and narrator voice.
- "scene" tells the illustrator what the picture shows (action, emotion, who is where), in {{ui_language}}.
- "characters" lists the bible ids of the characters visible in the picture.
- "composition": camera distance and layout in a few words. "text_zone" is "top" or "bottom": where the page text sits; the illustration keeps that third calm.
- Every scene must also work as colouring-book line art for this age: "coloring_scene" describes the simplified version (only the essential shapes, at most {{age_profile.max_focal}} focal elements).
- "objects" and "location" use ids from the Story Bible; "continuity" notes what must match the previous page.
Picture-book craft (apply it):
- Three movements with clear page ranges: beginning (setup, voice, rhythm), development (escalation: each beat a little bigger, with variation), climax and ending (surprising yet inevitable, then calm). One beat, one moment of change, per page.
- Repetition with variation and the rule of three (a refrain, three tries, three sounds) so the child can anticipate and join in.
- Page turns: mark 3-5 pages as "reveal" (the turn delivers a surprise or discovery) and the rest as "quiet"; never make every turn dramatic, and never let a turn feel unrelated to the page before.
- Reveal pacing: a key object or character must NOT appear before the page where it is discovered or introduced; list it in "must_not_show" on earlier pages.
- The main character initiates the key actions; secondary characters support and never take over.
- Clarity: no scene or phrase a parent could misread. When friends say good night, each goes to their OWN home or nest (with family if any); they never sleep together unless they are family and the story says so. Avoid ambiguous pronouns; name the character when two are present.
- Natural wording: no filler adjectives ("a small little puddle"), no redundant diminutives, no clichés; every word earns its place in the read-aloud rhythm.
- Every page states what each visible character DOES ("actions"), using only the ways of holding objects listed in its anatomy. One clear event per page; the physical cause and effect must make sense (no layered micro-hazards).
- Adjacent pages do different narrative jobs (e.g. rain begins on one page, the shelter response on the next).
- A new friendship needs visible beats: meet, share, invite, do something together; a returning friend is remembered, not met again.
- No procedural or adult "safety manual" language; safety lives inside the action.
- Light, sparkles and weather are "natural" unless the world rules say magic exists; say so in "effects".
- The last page states where each character ends up ("final_locations").
- End warmly and completely; no sequel teaser unless the cast plan explicitly needs it.
- For young ages, give most pages a sound word ("sound") and one gentle educational element (a content intention, never a developmental promise).

THIS VOLUME:
APPROVED EXAMPLES FROM EARLIER COLLECTIONS OF THIS PUBLISHER (for tone and quality only; never copy them; may be empty): {{examples}}
Write volume {{n}} of {{structure.volumes}}: "{{item.title}}".
VOLUME PLAN: {{item}}
CLIENT'S OWN STORY FOR THIS VOLUME (may be empty). If present it is the BASIS of this volume: keep its plot, characters, page order and best lines; improve wording, clarity and rhythm; follow the age profile (add a little gentle action only if the age profile asks for it): {{seed_story_for_volume}}
CAST PLAN FOR THIS VOLUME (follow it: the main character leads; introduce new characters warmly; when a character RETURNS, recall in one light touch who they are and what happened before, so a child who reads this volume alone still understands): {{cast_volume}}
WHAT HAPPENED BEFORE (continuity ledger so far, may be empty): {{continuity.ledger}}

prompts.visual_qa:
TASK: check a children's picture book page by page, like its Art Director.
You receive images in order. Character reference sheets first: {{refs_list}}. Then the book pages to check: {{pages_list}}.
For EACH page image check FOUR dimensions together (a page passes only if all four pass):
1. anatomy: every character matches its reference and anatomy (stance, limb count and attachment, extremity shape: e.g. no human-like hand or fingers on a quadruped, no extra limbs), and every invariant (exact spot count, horn count, frill, palette, proportions).
2. action: each character visibly does what "actions" says, in a physically believable way for its body (e.g. who holds the leaf, and how).
3. story: the page shows the scene and objects of the page contract, nothing listed in must_not_show, object invariants respected (e.g. the pebble stays smooth and shiny), no text or letters inside the image, no magic unless stated.
4. readability: one clear focal action a young child understands at a glance; background not so busy that it hides the action.
KNOWN FAILURE PATTERNS FROM REAL PAST ATTEMPTS (check each one explicitly; may be empty): {{known_failures}}
Ignore camera angle and background variations that do not break these rules.
For each page give ok, the four dimension results, short issues (in {{ui_language}}), and one precise redraw instruction in English that fixes ALL issues at once while keeping everything that is already correct.
